title: He Took Three Wickets and Scored 66 Off 34 Balls. At the Wankhede, Arjun Tendulkar Is Carving His Own Path.
excerpt: Sachin's son delivered a match-winning all-round performance in the T20 Mumbai League, then gave the signed match ball to a young fan his six had hit.
body:
He bowled three overs — one of them a maiden — and took 3 wickets for 11 runs. Then he walked out to bat, smashed 66 off 34 balls, and walked off unbeaten. On Monday evening at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai, Arjun Tendulkar delivered the kind of performance that would have made headlines no matter whose son he was.

In the Nuvama Private T20 Mumbai League 2026, Arjun's Arcs Andheri side demolished Bandra Blasters by nine wickets. The margin and the manner told the story: this was complete domination by a 26-year-old all-rounder who has spent years trying to step out from under the longest shadow in Indian cricket.

## The Bowling Spell

Arjun opened up with the ball and was immediately effective. His left-arm pace found sharp movement and consistent lines, dismantling the Bandra Blasters batting order. He finished with figures of 3/11 in three overs — an economy rate of 3.70 in a T20 where the format usually punishes anything under 8.

Bandra Blasters managed 144/9 in their 20 overs, with Om Keshkamat (49) and Sagarr Chhabriaa (44 not out) providing a late rescue act for the eighth wicket. But Arjun and fellow bowler Prasoon Singh (2/12) had already done the damage up top.

## The Chase

Chasing 145, Arcs Andheri lost Divyaansh Sksena early for 26. What followed was a partnership that turned a modest run chase into a statement. Arjun joined Musheer Khan at the crease, and the two left-handers put on an unbroken 116 runs for the second wicket.

Arjun's knock of 66 not out came off just 34 deliveries. He hit five sixes and four fours, striking at 194.12. Khan, no less fluent, scored 54 not out off 38. Together, they ensured the target was reached with nine wickets in hand and 37 balls to spare — the definition of a one-sided contest.

## The Gesture

During his knock, one of Arjun's sixes cleared the rope and struck a young fan in the stands. After the match, he sought out the child, checked on them, and gifted them the signed match ball — a small act that earned as much attention on social media as his batting had on the field. It was a reminder that at the Wankhede, the Tendulkar name has always meant more than just runs.

## Stepping Out of the Shadow

For Indian cricket fans in the diaspora, Arjun Tendulkar has always been a figure of curiosity. He is the son of Sachin Tendulkar — the man with 100 international centuries, 18,426 Test runs, and a World Cup winner's medal from 2011. Every ball Arjun bowls and every shot he plays is measured against a standard no cricketer in history has matched.

But Arjun, who plays for Goa in domestic cricket and the Lucknow Super Giants in the IPL, has never tried to replicate his father's game. He is a left-arm seamer who bats aggressively — a different profile, a different skill set, a different ambition. And on evenings like Monday at the Wankhede, the runs and wickets belong to him alone.

The T20 Mumbai League is not international cricket. But all-round performances of this calibre — 3/11 with the ball, 66 not out with the bat, in the same match, at the same venue where his father once defined an era — are how careers gather momentum. For NRIs following Indian cricket, Arjun's journey resonates deeply, as many feel the weight of family expectations and the desire to carve out their own identities abroad. This performance not only strengthens his position in Indian cricket but also serves as an inspiration for young Indians abroad who aspire to break free from familial legacies while pursuing their passions.
